resources.string: A little clarity in the noise.
Digital input, not physical sound pressure. Calibrate with a reference meter.
Single-point estimate. Accuracy varies by device and sound.

Use a reference sound level meter beside your phone. Match its frequency weighting, keep the sound steady, and enter its reading. Saving ends this session; the profile applies to the next measurement.
My reference meter uses the same weighting shown here.
Measure a steady sound for at least 3 seconds. Avoid silence and clipping.
Input changed. This profile does not apply to the current microphone or settings.
Only numeric levels and input settings are included. Audio is never recorded.

Sound is processed on your device. Microphone audio is never saved or uploaded, and measurements are never automatically uploaded. Calibration profiles and your last session stay on this device. Sharing a CSV sends only the file you choose through the app you select.

Optional. Firebase Crashlytics receives crash reports, app/device information and an installation identifier to help fix problems. Audio and sound levels are never included. You can turn this off at any time.

Without calibration, values are digital input levels (dBFS), not physical sound pressure. A reference calibration gives an estimate for that microphone, gain and setup only. This app is not a certified instrument and does not assess hearing, safe exposure time or legal compliance.

A weighting reduces low-frequency input. The digital filter is tested with tones from 31.5 Hz to 8 kHz; microphone response and very high frequencies still vary. Flat leaves the PCM unweighted. Statistics use 100 ms RMS windows and a sample-weighted energy average. The display floor is −120 dBFS. Sessions stop after 4 hours.
Allow microphone access to measure sound. Audio stays on your device and is never saved.

Sori uses the microphone to measure sound levels on your device. Audio is never saved or sent.
